scope: Complete literal mainspace wikitext only; source-bound regenerated plans; uncertainty preserves source without adding a generic alert.
compatibleExistingMigrations: Existing English Cite mappings and registered citation profiles only. A repaired foreign call must produce an unblocked established native migration. Legacy model and field changes are replayed and counted separately from every new finite value repair. Unknown profiles, conflicting fields and protected owners stay unchanged.
boundedComposition: A finite field repair may compose with an exact named-empty-field deletion already proved by the existing citation cleanup, preserving output-control flags. Those preverified empty fields cannot create false role conflicts. Nonempty unknown or conflicting fields remain blocked. One extra assignment is removed before a permitted quote/protocol repair only when the entire remaining typed value is admissible. Legacy value labels come from the exact source field and classify only real date fields as dates.

features.5: Remove one exact outer quote pair around one literal HTTP(S) citation URL, preserving its bytes.
features.6: Extract a validated PMID, PMC, arXiv version or DOI from a sole unlabelled official-domain external link.
features.7: Recover nome/grupo identity attributes only when a complete unique definition, unresolved native call and matching collector establish the exact target graph.
features.8: Close the sole unclosed ref only when its entire body is one complete accepted citation immediately before the sole matching final collector.
features.9: Unwrap a sole ISBN template with exactly one checksum-valid ISBN argument in an accepted ISBN field, preserving digits and separators.
features.10: Remove one extra leading assignment character only in accepted typed URL, identifier and unambiguous ISO date or year fields.
features.11: Remove the extra slash in a uniquely paired literal </ref/> closer. A remaining unclosed ref is allowed only through the separately regenerated exact final-citation proof.
features.14: Collapse two to four identical leading protocol prefixes in accepted URL roles. Mixed schemes, longer chains, credentials and inner path/query strings remain unchanged.
